newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.S. CPI triggers leap in S.African industrials.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CPI triggers leap in S.African industrials.

text.p: Better-than-expected U.S. inflation data triggered a leap in South African industrial shares in Tuesday afternoon trade, dealers said.
The local industrial index sprang to a day's high of 8,217.7 points, 50.9 points higher, after earlier trading in a stale and meagre range with a low of 8,170.9 points.
"It is on the U.S. CPI. It was much, much better than expected and bodes very well in the short-term," said James Scott, dealer at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
The South African stock market spent most of Tuesday trading warily ahead of the figure's release, aware that it would dictate to U.S. markets which in turn would call the shots for world markets.

Dealers said local industrials could move still higher on Tuesday but would take their final cue from Wall Street's open. That market suffered a 148-point plunge last Friday and positive news could allow it to repeat Monday's firmer finish.
"They could possibly go higher. The market will keep track of the Dow," one dealer said.
U.S. March Consumer Price inflation rose 0.1 percent compared to a 0.3 percent rise in February. Analysts had expected a 0.2 percent rise.
"The figure has managed to allay many fears of another 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates," Scott said.
